label: Farmers IoT — both sensors
info:
Receives readings from the water tank probe (Module 1) and the soil
probe (Module 2), and serves a live page at GET /page — one card per reporting node, so extra
soil beds appear on their own.

Works whether the two sensors are on one ESP8266 or two — each has its
own endpoint, so nothing cares where the POST came from.

SUPERSEDES flows/water-level-flow.json. Do not import both: two `http in`
nodes on /water will conflict.

Core nodes only — no node-red-dashboard install. Every extra install step
is a place a build dies on someone else's phone.

Test with no hardware at all:

    curl -X POST http://localhost:1880/water -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
         -d '{"node":"water-tank-1","ok":true,"raw":139,"depth_mm":113}'

    curl -X POST http://localhost:1880/soil -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
         -d '{"node":"soil-bed-1","ok":true,"moisture_pct":22.4,"temp_c":20.2,"ec":0}'

Then open http://<phone-ip>:1880/page in a browser.

name: READ ME — endpoints, payloads, and the one thing people forget
info:
ENDPOINTS
  POST /water            Module 1, the QDY30A tank probe
  POST /soil             Module 2, the THC-S soil probe
  GET  /valve            returns 1/0 — the node POLLS this for the valve
  POST /valve/set?v=1|0  the page Open/Close buttons set the desired state
  GET  /page             live page: a card per node + valve buttons

VALVE IS MANUAL FOR NOW: no moisture thresholds. The buttons set
flow.valveCmd; the node polls GET /valve every ~1s and drives the relay.
The node echoes its ACTUAL pin state back in the /soil payload as `valve`,
so the page can show confirmed vs commanded.

THE ONE THING PEOPLE FORGET: every `http in` needs an `http response`.
Without it the request never completes and the ESP blocks until timeout.

PUSH TO CLOUD — store-and-forward to farm-ingest
info:
The phone is behind carrier CGNAT, so nothing can dial IN to it. This group
dials OUT instead: readings are buffered in flow context and POSTed in batches
to the VPS. Survives 4G dropouts — nothing is deleted from the buffer until
the server has answered 200.

**Change the URL or token in the `drain outbox` function** — both live at the
top of that one node, nowhere else.

Both `http in` nodes feed `queue for cloud` directly rather than going through
the `store …` functions, because those return null on `ok:false` and the fault
rows are the ones you most want off the phone.

The push is EVENT-DRIVEN: every arriving reading triggers a drain. Android
freezes Termux's JS timers when the phone dozes, so a purely scheduled push
silently stops while everything still looks healthy. An ESP POST has already
woken the process, so draining on that event needs no wake-lock. The 30 s
inject is only a backstop for retrying while no new readings are arriving.

⚠️ The buffer lives in memory. A Node-RED restart drops whatever is queued.
To survive restarts, add a filesystem context store in settings.js.
